To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the anti-nonspecific binding properties of a glycocalyx-mimicking glycopolymer can be controlled by the chain density and the chain length.

the anti-nonspecific adsorption of proteins can be achieved with glycocalyx-like layers of high grafting density and that the amount adsorbed depends on the length of the chains as well as on the size of proteins.

a glycocalyx-mimicking layer of poly(GAMA) can be grafted from a mixed thiol SAM, that the grafting density and length of the chains are important for protein binding, and that the size of the adsorbing protein also plays a role.
In summary, our research is concerned with
mimicking the glycocalyx layer by a glycopolymer coating on solid surfaces.
the development of glycocalyx-like layers for biomaterials surfaces to overcome the problems associated with nonspecific protein adsorption.
the development of a glycocalyx-mimicking surface that resists the nonspecific adsorption of proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the higher the density of glycopolymeric chains on the surface, the higher the resistance to nonspecific protein adsorption, and that the resistance to protein adsorption is also affected by the length of the glycopolymers and the protein size.
the glycocalyx-like poly(GAMA) layer is a promising tool to prevent nonspecific protein adsorption on surfaces.
the glycocalyx-like surface layer can be successfully imitated by a glycopolymer brush layer and that this layer can be used to resist nonspecific protein adsorption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anti-nonspecific adsorption properties of the glycoprotein layers are influenced by the chain density and the size of the protein.
the anti-nonspecific adsorption behavior of a glycopolymer can be tuned by controlling the grafting density and chain length of the glycopolymers and the size of the protein.
the anti-nonspecific binding properties are dependent on both the density and the chain length of the glycopolymers and also on the protein size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glycocalyx-like poly(GAMA) layer is able to resist nonspecific protein adsorption, which is of importance in many applications.
the glycocalyx-like poly(GAMA) layer is able to reduce protein adsorption, and that the anti-adsorptive behavior depends on the chain density of the glycoconjugate and the size of the protein.
a biomimetic glycocalyxl-like glycopolymeric layer can be prepared by surface-initiated ATRA and that the glycopolymeric layers are resistant to protein adsorptions.
